games.title: Basketball points
games.body_md:
Four friends recorded how many points they scored in four basketball games.

| Player | Game 1 | Game 2 | Game 3 | Game 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Asha | 6 | 8 | 5 | 9 |
| Ben | 7 | 7 | 9 | 6 |
| Cody | 10 | 4 | 6 | 8 |
| Dina | 5 | 9 | 8 | 8 |

questions.home: Read the question for what to compare (a whole day, a whole person) before looking at the numbers. Sports tables and weather data are great practice.
questions.prompt_md: Who scored the most points altogether?
questions.solution_md:
Add each row:

- Asha: $6+8+5+9 = 28$
- Ben: $7+7+9+6 = 29$
- Cody: $10+4+6+8 = 28$
- Dina: $5+9+8+8 = 30$

Dina scored the most.

questions.home: Write each step as a line (1 gem = 3 gold, 1 gold = 4 silver …) and multiply down the chain. Kitchen measures (cups, tablespoons, teaspoons) are good real-life practice.
questions.prompt_md:
3 small boxes fit exactly inside 1 medium box. 4 medium boxes fit exactly inside 1 large box.

How many small boxes fit inside 2 large boxes?
questions.solution_md: 1 large box holds 4 medium boxes $= 4 \times 3 = 12$ small boxes. So 2 large boxes hold $2 \times 12 = 24$.

questions.home: Draw a line from tallest to shortest and place one name per clue, starting with the clue that links to the most others. Logic puzzle books help a lot.
questions.prompt_md:
Four children compare their heights.

- Ali is taller than Bo.
- Cy is shorter than Bo.
- Di is taller than Ali.

Who is the second tallest?
questions.solution_md:
Put them in order from the clues: Di > Ali (clue 3), Ali > Bo (clue 1), Bo > Cy (clue 2).

Order from tallest: Di, **Ali**, Bo, Cy.

questions.home: Draw a bar for the whole amount and shade each fraction as it's spent. Watch for 'of what was left', which is a fraction of the remainder, not of the whole.
questions.prompt_md:
Jess spent half of her money on a book. Then she spent half of what was left on a drink. She has \$5 left.

How much money did she start with?
questions.solution_md:
Work backwards. Before the drink she had $\$5 \times 2 = \$10$. Before the book she had $\$10 \times 2 = \$20$.

Check: half of \$20 is \$10; half of \$10 is \$5, leaving \$5. ✓

questions.home: Build the first few shapes with toothpicks, write the counts in a table, and find what gets added each time. Then predict the 10th and check it.
questions.prompt_md:
Matchsticks are used to make triangles in a row, each one sharing a side with the next:

- 1 triangle uses 3 matchsticks.
- 2 triangles use 5 matchsticks.
- 3 triangles use 7 matchsticks.

How many matchsticks are needed for 10 triangles?
questions.solution_md:
The first triangle uses 3 matchsticks and each new one adds 2.

10 triangles: $3 + 9 \times 2 = 21$.

questions.home: Remember triangles add to 180° and four-sided shapes to 360°. Call the smallest angle s and write the others using s.
questions.prompt_md:
The angles in a triangle add up to 180°. A triangle has one right angle (90°), and its other two angles are equal.

What is the size of each of the other two angles?
questions.solution_md: The other two angles share $180 - 90 = 90°$. Equal shares: $90 \div 2 = 45°$.

questions.home: List in an order (biggest first digit to smallest) so nothing is missed or counted twice, and look for the pattern in the counts.
questions.prompt_md: How many two-digit numbers have digits that add up to 5?

questions.home: Count multiples by dividing (how many 6s fit into 100). For 'divisible by both', use the lowest common multiple, not just the two numbers multiplied.
questions.prompt_md: How many whole numbers from 1 to 30 can be divided exactly by 3 but **not** by 2?
questions.solution_md:
Multiples of 3 up to 30: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30 (10 numbers).

Take away the even ones (6, 12, 18, 24, 30). That leaves 3, 9, 15, 21, 27: **5**.

questions.home: Work out which ingredient runs out first. Scaling a recipe when you're short of one ingredient is perfect practice.
questions.prompt_md:
One batch of pancakes needs 3 eggs and 2 cups of flour. Sam has 10 eggs and 8 cups of flour.

What is the greatest number of full batches Sam can make?
questions.solution_md:
Eggs: 10 eggs is enough for 3 batches (9 eggs), with 1 egg left over.

Flour: 8 cups is enough for 4 batches.

The eggs run out first, so Sam can make **3** batches.

questions.home: Draw a timeline (years ago, now, years ahead) and test the options. Make up age puzzles about the family.
questions.prompt_md: Ella is 6 and her mum is 30. In how many years will her mum be exactly 3 times as old as Ella?
questions.solution_md:
Try the options. In 6 years Ella will be 12 and her mum will be 36. $36 = 3 \times 12$. ✓

(In 2 years: 8 and 32, which is 4 times. In 4 years: 10 and 34, not 3 times.)
